behaviours.excerpt: Near-misses and other thermal events without a credible safety risk must be recorded and included in quarterly regulator summaries.
behaviours.comparison: Shared-benefit section (both companies have unreported incidents). Non-serious thermal events are deferred to quarterly summaries (later than 30 days) and customer notice is limited to events with a credible safety risk. This is weaker than the acceptable range (reporting within <=30 days; customer notice within <=45 days; minor events not excluded).

behaviours.excerpt: A failure rate above 5% triggers regulator review and a corrective-action plan, not automatic exclusion from sale. Regulators may require retesting, additional safeguards, or a time-limited sales restriction
behaviours.comparison: S2 is weakened below the acceptable range (no mandatory stop to above-limit sales; sales restriction discretionary) and benefits Northwind (Hearth 10 at 6.2%). Paired with the S5 loosening in m14 (recall reduced to regulator assessment, benefiting Halcyon's Ember 8 at 9.9), this is an implicit trade of two weakened sections, each benefiting one company.

behaviours.excerpt: Regulators must assess a model for mandatory recall when verified thermal incidents exceed 8 per 100,000 installed units in a year
behaviours.comparison: S5 is weakened below the acceptable range: a >8 per 100,000 incident rate triggers only assessment, not a mandatory recall, with recall left to regulator or manufacturer discretion. This benefits Halcyon (Ember 8 at 9.9). It is paired with the S2 loosening in m13 that benefits Northwind, forming an implicit cross-section trade.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal event involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled overheating, injury, property damage, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 72 hours of learning of it, with a complete report within 30 days. Near-misses and other thermal events without a credible safety risk must be recorded and included in quarterly regulator summaries.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A failure rate above 5% triggers regulator review and a corrective-action plan, not automatic exclusion from sale. Manufacturers must submit per-model results and corrective-action plans to regulators and provide each model's actual test results directly to prospective and current customers, along with relevant safety findings and protective instructions.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units manufactured 24 months after adoption must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and a means to notify the household when shut-off occurs. Manufacturers must retrofit compatible installed units, or provide an equivalent safety upgrade, within six years of adoption.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. The requirement applies to units manufactured on or after that date.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When verified thermal incidents for any model exceed 8 per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator, begin a recall, and provide customers with protective instructions; the regulator may set the recall scope and oversee implementation. A recall is also required whenever the regulator determines that a serious safety hazard warrants one, regardless of the incident-rate threshold.

document.section_notes: S2 converts the 5% figure from a sales ban into a regulator-review trigger with no mandatory sales stop, and per-model results go to customers and regulators but not to the public. S3 sets the new-unit shut-off deadline at 24 months (outside the 12-month acceptable range) while the six-year retrofit stays within bounds. S5 adopts a mandatory 8-per-100,000 recall trigger with no transition, which bears directly on Halcyon's Ember 8 at 9.9. S1's quarterly reporting for events without credible risk is the 90-day figure I recorded; the text sets no explicit deadline for those events, so this is an interpretive extraction.
